claims: n147_S65104355.json is an exact rational certificate of 147 unit squares, each its centre (cx, cy) in [0, S]^2 and t = tan(theta/2), in a square of rational side S whose 12-place ceiling #985 prints as the bound, 12.651043556588; the issue also prints the exact side to 30 places, 12.651043556587694471904370629016..., and states that it is 0.005810692904685 below the registry's 12.65685424949238 (= 7 + 4 sqrt(2)), read at main fa980f8e. evidence/registration/n147.cert is the same packing as text. n147.strict.cert and n147.strict.json are the packing moved by (1e-15, 1e-15) in a square of side S + 2e-15. The issue says the packing touches the four walls. Feasibility only: no optimality, KKT or rigidity claim.

The issue reports the author's runs of verify.py (all 10731 pairs) VALID, indep_check.py (328 close pairs) PASSED and fu_strict_check.py on the strict copy STRICT VALID, least pair margin 3.003e-10, least wall margin 1e-15, with the same statement of what the checkers share as #984's. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.

The issue discloses first that the packing does not beat the Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard's side-only entry at 147, 12.651043553172632772258400... (team Nevska, 7 November), 3.415e-09 below this side, which supplies no packing. Its lineage: the registry's n = 229 record (Evan Daniel, 2026-10-20, side 15.6501615138764..., W-known-best-n229), a three-wide diagonal band of tilted squares between two corner-anchored grids, with every square of 13 <= x + y < 19 deleted and the squares beyond moved by (-3, -3), removing one period of the band; 147 squares overlap by at most 0.010 and a penalty step and an exact-constraint sequential-LP polish (search/opt.py) remove the overlaps at a cost of 0.00088 in side. It says other cuts and seven other copies or versions of the n = 229 packing give 12.651043557 to 12.651056453, that the registry's n = 147 packing, the 45-degree arrangement shared with n = 148, is a different arrangement, asks that Daniel's n = 229 packing be credited as the start and Roberto Ono as the credit name, and says the packing was found by an AI coding agent (Claude, by Anthropic) directed by a person.
